LESSON: WOOD WORKING JOINTS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: General
Strand: Wood Processes and Products
Topic 3.2: Wood working joints
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 26

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Wood working joints, part of Wood Processes and Products in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 General.

Key inquiry question: How are wood joints constructed? 2. Why are wood fasteners important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Wood working joints together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: learner develops speaking, listening and teamwork skills when discussing

classification of wood working joints.

• Learning to Learn: learner reflects on their own work when visiting nearby wood workshops to observe/listen to the

application of wood joints.

• Digital Literacy: learner develops digital skills when interacting and manipulating digital devices when watching and

listening to video clips on how to prepare and assemble different woodworking joints

Values:
• Unity: learner collaborate with others as they construct woodworking joints

• Respect: learner appreciate each other’s contribution when discussing classification of wood working joints

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and security: learner handles tools to fabricate and strengthen joints.

Suggested Resources: workshop, joints, magnifying tools, tactile models, video clips, screws, nails, dowels

Key Concepts/Skills:

Identifying different types of joints in woodwork

Preparing joints used in woodwork
